title: Next batch decision (inner-loop step 13b: which samples run next, or stop)
description: Stage contract for inner-loop step 13b of PRECISION_GREASE_DEV, the sequential decision taken after a bench round. It decides two things at once. (i) Which samples the NEXT round runs: every proposed sample must name the competing hypotheses it separates, because the whole point of the inner loop is that the next batch is chosen to be informative, and a sample that cannot separate two competing explanations is not worth a bench slot. (ii) Whether the loop continues at all: stop_state carries the same six values as campaign.schema.json's iteration stop_state, and any value other than CONTINUE must record its reason in stop_rationale (see the if/then rule), because stopping the loop is a decision that needs its reason recorded exactly like continuing does. information_gain_basis states why these are the informative samples rather than others; bench_slots_required is what the round costs.

allOf.$comment: Stopping the loop is a decision like any other: a stop_state other than CONTINUE requires a non-empty stop_rationale, so no round can end the loop without a recorded reason.

campaign_reference.description: Campaign (inner-loop carrier) this round belongs to. The iteration history and its stop_state sequence live on that campaign; this record is the decision for one round boundary.

from_iteration.description: Bench round just completed, 1-based. Strictly positive.

to_iteration.description: Bench round this decision opens, 1-based. Strictly positive.

proposed_samples.description: Samples the next round would run. minItems 1: a next-batch decision that proposes nothing can only be a stop, and that stop is expressed by stop_state. Every entry names the competing hypotheses it separates, so a bench slot is never spent on a sample that cannot discriminate.

information_gain_basis.description: Why these are the informative samples rather than the alternatives considered: what the round buys that the previous round did not settle.

bench_slots_required.description: Bench slots the next round consumes if it runs. Strictly positive.

stop_state.description: How this round boundary ends: CONTINUE (another round is planned), GOAL_MET, NO_NEW_INFORMATION, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, PIVOT or KILL. Same six values as campaign.schema.json's iteration stop_state; only CONTINUE authorizes another round, and every other value requires stop_rationale.

stop_rationale.description: Why the loop stops. Hard-required and non-empty whenever stop_state is not CONTINUE (see the if/then rule); omitted when the loop continues, so no stop can be recorded without its cause.

proposed_sample.description: One sample the next round would run. It must name the hypothesis it discriminates and the pair of competing hypotheses it separates: a sample that cannot separate two competing explanations is not worth a bench slot. sample_reference and formula_reference are alternatives -- a sample that exists already is named by reference, while a formula the next round has yet to produce is named by its formula reference; at least one of the two must be present.

hypothesis.description: The hypothesis this sample is run to discriminate.

discriminates.description: The pair of competing hypotheses this sample separates (for example 'A explains the result' vs 'B explains the result').

next_round_budget.description: Optional remaining inner-loop budget at this round boundary. Both figures are recorded together when the object is present, so the next round can be checked against what is left of the campaign allowance.

bench_slots_remaining.description: Bench slots left for this campaign after the next round. Never negative.

calendar_days_remaining.description: Calendar days left for this campaign after the next round. Never negative.
